name: Windows BOF - Step 2: EIP Control (Pattern Offset)
description: Send a de Bruijn cyclic pattern instead of 'A's. When the service crashes, read the 4-byte value in EIP from Immunity Debugger and feed it to pattern_offset to find the exact number of bytes before EIP — the offset. Confirm by sending offset bytes of 'A', then 'BBBB' (42424242) in EIP, and padding after.
source: OSCP Classic - Windows Buffer Overflow Methodology

examples.label: Generate a cyclic pattern (use crash length + 400 bytes padding)
Find exact offset from EIP value seen in Immunity
Confirm control: 'A'*offset + 'B'*4 + 'C'*rest
examples.command: # EIP should show 42424242 (BBBB) on crash -> offset is correct

examples.label: Alternative: mona in Immunity Debugger
examples.command:
!mona pc 2400     # create pattern
!mona po 39694438  # find offset

notes: Make the pattern longer than your fuzz crash length to be safe (add 400 bytes). After finding the offset, ALWAYS confirm it: send exactly offset 'A's + 'BBBB' + 'C's to fill the rest — if EIP = 42424242 you have clean control. Mona (!mona pc / !mona po) is the Immunity-native equivalent of msf-pattern_* and works without switching windows. [Note: BOF labs removed from PEN-200 2024 curriculum but remain in OSCP practice machines and TryHackMe/HackTheBox prep.]

recommended.note: Fuzzing gives you the approximate crash length needed here.
With EIP confirmed, identify which bytes corrupt the stack.

defense.why_it_works: After fuzzing identifies the crash offset, a cyclic pattern (Metasploit pattern_create or cyclic) is sent to determine the exact byte offset at which the saved EIP is overwritten. When the application crashes, the unique 4-byte value in EIP maps back to an exact offset in the pattern. This gives the precise number of bytes of padding needed before the 4-byte return address override — enabling controlled EIP overwrite to redirect execution.
defense.prerequisites: Confirmed buffer overflow from fuzzing phase. Immunity Debugger + Mona.py on test system. Metasploit pattern_create tool. Exact offset value needed before crafting working exploit.
defense.impact: T1203 Exploitation for Client Execution. Precise EIP control enables redirection of execution to attacker-controlled shellcode. This is the core primitive for exploiting a stack buffer overflow into arbitrary code execution.
defense.detection:
Same as fuzzing — application crash with a recognizable cyclic pattern in EIP is a strong indicator of active exploit development. WER/crash dumps. IDS: malformed input with Metasploit cyclic pattern bytes (Aa0A, Aa1A... are recognizable patterns).
Client app (browser, Office, PDF/reader) crashes or loads from unusual location, then drops/modifies files in user-writable paths, spawns unexpected child (powershell/cmd/mshta/rundll32), and establishes outbound C2-like connections; correlate app logs, file writes, process lineage, and network egress (DET0287/AN0797).
Browser/Office/reader process logs crash/segfault; new executable/script in /sessions/magical-confident-franklin (Downloads, ~/.cache, /tmp); unexpected child like curl/wget/bash opens network connections (AN0798).
App crash in unified logs for Safari/Chrome/Office/Preview; new files in ~/Library, ~/Downloads, /private/var/folders/*; unexpected child (osascript, zsh, bash, curl) spawned; new outbound connections (AN0799).
defense.artifacts: Application crash (Event 1000) | WER crash dump containing cyclic pattern | IDS: Metasploit cyclic pattern string in input | Debugger: specific cyclic 4-byte value in EIP register
defense.prevention:
Stack canaries detect overwrite before EIP is reached. DEP/NX prevents execution of injected shellcode. ASLR randomizes return address — even with EIP control, return address must be known. CFG (Control Flow Guard): validates indirect call targets.
Application Isolation and Sandboxing: Browser sandboxes can mitigate exploitation impact; other virtualization/microsegmentation may also help.
Exploit Protection: Use WDEG/EMET to mitigate exploitation behavior; control flow integrity checking can identify and stop software exploits.
Update Software: Perform regular software updates to mitigate exploitation risk.
defense.evasion: Generate a custom (non-Metasploit) cyclic pattern to evade signature detection on the pattern bytes. Target offline test environment. Use non-standard input vector.
defense.misconfiguration: No stack canary: EIP overwrite reaches saved return address undetected. ASLR disabled: return addresses are predictable. No CFG: arbitrary EIP redirection succeeds without control flow validation.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Verify no stack canary (Immunity Debugger/mona):
# !mona modules
# → GS: False (no stack canary) for vulnerable module
# → ASLR: False (fixed base address)
# → Rebase: False
# → SafeSEH: False
# → NXCompat: False
# ALL False = fully exploitable
defense.secure_config:
# Enable all binary mitigations:
# cl.exe /GS /DYNAMICBASE /NXCOMPAT /GUARD:cf vuln.c

# Verify mitigations on existing binary:
# PowerShell:
$binary = 'C:\Program Files\App\app.exe'
$pe = [System.Reflection.Assembly]::LoadFile($binary)
# Or use:
# Get-PEHeader $binary | Select-Object ASLR, DEP, SafeSEH, CFGuard

# Process Mitigation Policy via PowerShell:
Set-ProcessMitigation -Name app.exe -Enable DEP,ASLR,StrictHandleChecks,CFG
